ionSum.sumHelp: Excludes pH and any disabled channel. Excludes unmeasured anions (sulfate, phosphate, bicarbonate).
ionSum.ecHelp: Range uses TDS↔EC factor 0.55–0.75 for mixed hydroponic salts. Compare to your handheld EC meter.
ionSum.howTo: How to use this: if your handheld EC meter reads within the bracket above ({{low}}–{{high}} dS/m), the AMIC's ion concentrations are consistent with the actual feed. A handheld reading below the range = unmeasured anions or AMIC over-reading. Above the range = sample dilution, sample line on the wrong source, or AMIC under-reading.

pump.title: Pump Timing
pump.help: Sample-in / sample-out durations during a Measure cycle. Increase input if the cell isn't fully covering both probes (manual p.11). Spec defaults: 12 s / 16 s.
pump.saved: Pump times saved: input {{input}} s · output {{output}} s

history.title: Cycle History
history.help: The pH-probe live mV is sampled every ~15 s during each cycle. Calibration uses the multi-ion standards (P1 Low, P2 High), which usually differ in pH by 1–2 units — so a healthy Cal trace shows a ~30–120 mV swing as the cell drains, refills with the next standard, and the probe sees a different pH. A flat trace (under 5 mV swing) means the probe wasn't picking up either standard — cell didn't fill or there's air between the probe rods. (Note: the ~170 mV swing only applies to the manual pH calibration procedure with pH 4 / pH 7 buffers, not the automatic Calibration cycle.)
history.empty: No cycles recorded yet. The next Measure / Calibration / etc will be logged here when it completes.

dx.flatNoContact: flat — probe likely NOT in contact with liquid
dx.lowSwing: low swing ({{mv}} mV) — minimal solution change detected, contact suspect
dx.healthy: healthy {{mv}} mV swing — pH probe responding to standards

ph.title: pH Calibration
ph.help: 2-point calibration with pH 4.0 and pH 7.0 buffer solutions. The automatic calibration cycle does NOT calibrate pH.
ph.liveHelp: Updates with each status refresh. Wait for the value to stabilize before capturing.
ph.buffersHelp: Choose the calibration buffers you actually have on hand. The AMIC firmware natively expects pH 4.0 / pH 7.0; for any other pair, SenseHub adds a display offset and records it with each saved measurement.
ph.spanWarning: Buffer span isn't 3 pH units apart — calibration may be slightly off-slope. Standard pairs (4↔7 or 7↔10) work best.
ph.invalidBuffers: Set valid buffer pH values (low < high) before capturing
ph.confirmCapture:
Capture current pH probe reading ({{mv}} mV) as the {{label}} calibration point?

Make sure the probe is in the correct buffer solution and the reading has stabilized.

This will also save buffer values pH {{low}} / {{high}} to SenseHub.
ph.step1Body: Remove the pH and Multi-Ion probes from the measurement cell (per the manual's Probes Installation section). Don't touch the tips.
ph.step2Body: Place both probes in a container with pH {{ph}} buffer solution. Wait for the live reading above to stabilize (typically 30-60 seconds).
ph.step3Body: Take both probes out, rinse with deionized water, dry gently with tissue paper. Don't touch the tips.
ph.step4Body: Place both probes in pH {{ph}} buffer solution. Wait for the reading to stabilize.
ph.step5Body: Rinse, dry, and reinstall both probes back into the measurement cell. The next Run Measurement will use the new pH calibration.
ph.step5BodyOffset: Rinse, dry, and reinstall both probes back into the measurement cell. The next Run Measurement will use the new pH calibration with a {{offset}} pH display offset applied by SenseHub.
